passages.text: The elder, To the chosen lady and her children, whom I love in the truth—and not I alone, but also all who know the truth— because of the truth that abides in us and will be with us forever: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, will be with us in truth and love.
passages.sermon:
The elder writes this letter.
He writes to the chosen lady and to her children.
I love you in the truth.
I am not the only one who loves you.
All who know the truth also love you.
We love you because the truth lives in us.
The truth will be with us forever.
Grace will be with us.
Mercy will be with us.
Peace will be with us.
These come from God the Father.
They also come from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father.
We will have these blessings in truth and love.
passages.original: Ὁ πρεσβύτερος Ἐκλεκτῇ κυρίᾳ καὶ τοῖς τέκνοις αὐτῆς οὓς ἐγὼ ἀγαπῶ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ καὶ οὐκ ἐγὼ μόνος ἀλλὰ καὶ πάντες οἱ ἐγνωκότες τὴν ἀλήθειαν διὰ τὴν ἀλήθειαν τὴν μένουσαν ἐν ἡμῖν καὶ μεθ’ ἡμῶν ἔσται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα Ἔσται μεθ’ ἡμῶν χάρις ἔλεος εἰρήνη παρὰ Θεοῦ Πατρός καὶ παρὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Πατρός ἐν ἀληθείᾳ καὶ ἀγάπῃ

passages.text: I was overjoyed to find some of your children walking in the truth, just as the Father has commanded us.
passages.sermon:
I am the elder.
I write to the chosen lady and her children.
I was very glad.
I found some of your children.
They are walking in the truth.
God the Father has commanded us to walk in the truth.
passages.original: Ἐχάρην λίαν ὅτι εὕρηκα ἐκ τῶν τέκνων σου περιπατοῦντας ἐν ἀληθείᾳ καθὼς ἐντολὴν ἐλάβομεν παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός

passages.text: And now I urge you, dear lady—not as a new commandment to you, but one we have had from the beginning—that we love one another.
passages.sermon:
I speak to you now, chosen lady.
I do not give you a new command.
This command is not new.
We have had this command from the beginning.
The command is this: We must love one another.
passages.original: καὶ νῦν ἐρωτῶ σε κυρία οὐχ ὡς ἐντολὴν γράφων σοι καινὴν ἀλλὰ ἣν εἴχομεν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ἵνα ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους

passages.text: And this is love, that we walk according to His commandments. This is the very commandment you have heard from the beginning, that you must walk in love.
passages.sermon:
Love means obeying God’s commandments.
God commands us to walk in His ways.
You have heard this commandment from the beginning.
God commands you to walk in love.
passages.original: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἀγάπη ἵνα περιπατῶμεν κατὰ τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ αὕτη ἡ ἐντολή ἐστιν καθὼς ἠκούσατε ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ἵνα ἐν αὐτῇ περιπατῆτε

passages.text: For many deceivers have gone out into the world, refusing to confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh. Any such person is the deceiver and the antichrist.
passages.sermon:
Many deceivers have gone out into the world.
These people do not confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh.
Anyone who does not confess this is a deceiver.
Anyone who does not confess this is the antichrist.
passages.original: Ὅτι πολλοὶ πλάνοι ἐξῆλθον εἰς τὸν κόσμον οἱ μὴ ὁμολογοῦντες Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐρχόμενον ἐν σαρκί οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ πλάνος καὶ ὁ ἀντίχριστος

passages.text: Watch yourselves, so that you do not lose what we have worked for, but that you may be fully rewarded.
passages.sermon:
You must watch yourselves.
You must be careful.
Do not lose what we have worked for.
We have worked for your faith and obedience.
If you are careful, you will receive a full reward.
passages.original: βλέπετε ἑαυτούς ἵνα μὴ ἀπολέσητε ἃ εἰργασάμεθα ἀλλὰ μισθὸν πλήρη ἀπολάβητε

passages.text: Anyone who runs ahead without remaining in the teaching of Christ does not have God. Whoever remains in His teaching has both the Father and the Son.
passages.sermon:
Anyone who does not remain in the teaching of Christ does not have God.
Anyone who goes beyond the teaching of Christ does not have God.
Anyone who remains in the teaching of Christ has God.
This person has both the Father and the Son.
passages.original: πᾶς ὁ προάγων καὶ μὴ μένων ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ τοῦ Χριστοῦ Θεὸν οὐκ ἔχει ὁ μένων ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ οὗτος καὶ τὸν Πατέρα καὶ τὸν Υἱὸν ἔχει

passages.text: If anyone comes to you but does not bring this teaching, do not receive him into your home or even greet him.
passages.sermon:
John wrote this letter to Christians.
He warned them about false teachers.
He said, "If anyone comes to you and does not bring the teaching of Christ, do not receive that person into your home."
Do not greet that person.
passages.original: Εἴ τις ἔρχεται πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ταύτην τὴν διδαχὴν οὐ φέρει μὴ λαμβάνετε αὐτὸν εἰς οἰκίαν καὶ χαίρειν αὐτῷ μὴ λέγετε

passages.text: Whoever greets such a person shares in his evil deeds.
passages.sermon:
This statement warns about greeting false teachers.
\r\nA false teacher does not bring the teaching of Christ.
\r\nAnyone who greets a false teacher shares in his evil deeds.
passages.original: ὁ λέγων γὰρ αὐτῷ χαίρειν κοινωνεῖ τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ τοῖς πονηροῖς

passages.text: I have many things to write to you, but I would prefer not to do so with paper and ink. Instead, I hope to come and speak with you face to face, so that our joy may be complete.
passages.sermon:
I have many things to write to you.
I do not want to write them with paper and ink.
I hope to come to you.
I want to speak with you face to face.
Then our joy will be complete.
passages.original: Πολλὰ ἔχων ὑμῖν γράφειν οὐκ ἐβουλήθην διὰ χάρτου καὶ μέλανος ἀλλὰ ἐλπίζω γενέσθαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ στόμα πρὸς στόμα λαλῆσαι ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ ἡμῶν πεπληρωμένη ᾖ

passages.text: The children of your elect sister send you greetings.
passages.sermon: The children greet you.\r\nThese children belong to your sister.\r\nYour sister is chosen by God.
passages.original: Ἀσπάζεταί σε τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἀδελφῆς σου τῆς ἐκλεκτῆς
